newsitem.title: UK: Low margins push Elf into British refinery linkup.
newsitem.headline: Low margins push Elf into British refinery linkup.

text.p: French oil giant Elf said Wednesday it was merging its British refining and retail operations with units of two U.S. oil companies in a $5 billion deal.

Elf said it hoped to finalise the deal with Chevron Corp. subsidiary Gulf Oil and Murco Petroleum, a unit of Murphy Oil Corp., early next year in a link-up that would shut Gulf's 115,000 barrels per day British refinery in Pembroke, south Wales.
"The difficulties currently faced by the oil refining and marketing industry are well known," said Elf Oil U.K.'s managing director Christian Cleret.
"We recognise today that, for all three of us, this merger is the best option for a promising future as a new force to be reckoned with in the U.K. market."

Oversupply of refined products, the growing cost of meeting tough environmental regulations and fierce competition in the retail gasoline market from oil majors like Exxon and supermarket chains forced Elf's hand, industry analysts said.
"Companies are just not prepared to throw good money after bad in refining investment," said Salomon Brothers analyst Jeremy Hudson.
Analysts said the merger, which follows a similar Europe-wide link-up between British Petroleum and Mobil in February, was unlikely to be the last given the sector's bleak outlook.
"There are quite a few smaller players who must be feeling uncomfortable in the current market," said Morgan Stanley energy analyst Chris Buckley.
"The fact that Elf has acted in this way and that Chevron is a party to this shows how bad conditions have got," said Salomon's Hudson.

The merger, which will create a retail network of about 1,500 service stations with an estimated 8 percent share of the British fuels market, would help reduce refining overcapacity and cut the companies' cost by about 50 million pounds ($ million) a year.

Elf expects the move will cost 400-500 jobs -- about a third of the partners' total work force -- mainly in south Wales, as the new joint venture concentrates refining at an existing Elf/Murphy refinery in Milford Haven from the middle of 1997.

The new company, in which Elf and Gulf will each hold 41.25 percent and Murco 17.5 percent, will market all three brand names for both fuel and lubricants in the short-term but could later unify under a single brand, Elf said.
